title: Lock Day 0 Design Principles
summary: Fixed the six principles every later decision is measured against, before any hardware was racked.
details: No open ports on the home router, all external access outbound only
Network critical services kept off the high churn GPU node
ZFS replication with a bounded data loss window instead of shared storage
GPU passed through to a VM for both inference and transcoding
Services isolated in LXCs with Docker inside where needed
Website deployments immutable, SHA tagged images from CI/CD

title: Three Node Topology and Role Assignment
summary: Assigned each node a role matched to its hardware rather than fitting hardware to a predetermined role.
details: Node 1 as GPU compute on the OptiPlex 7070 MT
Node 2 as primary services on the 64GB EliteDesk
Node 3 as supporting services plus the third quorum vote
DNS placed on Node 3 to survive Node 1 reboot churn during passthrough work
Logical architecture diagram drafted

title: Node 1 CPU Selection
summary: The single open equipment decision. Replace the i9-9900 with a 6C/6T part to cut sustained power on a GPU bound workload.
details: Candidates narrowed to i5-9400 non F and i5-8500, both on Dell's supported list
Confirmed Q370 and LGA1151 carry microcode for either, so no BIOS gamble
Established that the gain comes from fewer cores, not the shared 65W TDP rating
Ruled out the 9400F, which drops the UHD 630 the design depends on
Decision deferred to price and availability

title: 500W PSU Swap via ATX Adapter
summary: Replace the stock 260W Dell unit, which cannot feed the Quadro P4000 under combined CPU and GPU load.
details: Fit the proprietary 6 pin to standard ATX adapter already on hand
Install the 500W ATX supply in the 7070 MT chassis
Verify rail stability under simultaneous CPU and GPU load

title: Install Replacement CPU
summary: Drop in whichever of the two candidate i5 parts wins on price, then confirm the platform boots clean.
details: Verify the part is the plain SKU with UHD 630, not an F variant
Reseat cooler and confirm POST without a BIOS update
Baseline idle and sustained package power against the i9-9900

title: Quadro P4000 PCIe Passthrough
summary: Bind the workstation card to a VM while keeping the integrated UHD 630 driving the host console.
details: Enable VT-d and configure IOMMU groups on the Proxmox host
Blacklist host drivers and bind the P4000 to vfio-pci
Confirm the UHD 630 still provides a permanent host console after handoff
Validate no Code 43 or reset behaviour, the reason a workstation card was chosen

title: Proxmox VE 9.2 Base Install
summary: Stand up the primary services node first, since it anchors ingress and CI/CD for everything else.
details: Install Proxmox VE 9.2 on Debian 13 Trixie
Create the local ZFS pool
Configure 1GbE networking and host naming

title: Cloudflare Tunnel and Reverse Proxy
summary: Establish the only external access path, an outbound tunnel with zero forwarded ports on the router.
details: Deploy Nginx Proxy Manager in an LXC
Bring up the Cloudflare Tunnel connector as outbound only
Route proxied traffic through to Node 1 and Node 3
Confirm the router still has no inbound port forwards

title: Gitea, Actions Runner, and Astro Deploy
summary: Immutable site deployments built in CI and shipped as SHA tagged images, using the node's 64GB of headroom.
details: Deploy Gitea and register the Actions runner
Build the Astro site in CI and tag images by commit SHA
Size Docker build cache against available memory
Verify concurrent Git operations and builds do not contend

title: Cluster Join and Third Quorum Vote
summary: Without the third vote the cluster cannot reach consensus and HA will not function.
details: Install Proxmox VE 9.2 and join the existing cluster
Verify Corosync heartbeat across all three nodes
Confirm quorum survives a single node reboot

title: Pi-hole DNS on the Low Churn Node
summary: DNS deliberately lands here so Node 1 reboots during passthrough work never take the whole network down.
details: Deploy Pi-hole in an LXC for DNS level ad blocking
Leave DHCP on the router to avoid a dual DHCP conflict
Point cluster hosts at the new resolver

title: Supporting Service Stack
summary: The lighter services that fit comfortably in 16GB alongside the quorum role.
details: Uptime Kuma for availability monitoring
Homepage as the service dashboard
Diun for container image update notifications
Vaultwarden for credential storage
Paperless-ngx for document management

title: Switch and 2.5GbE Uplink
summary: One switch carrying a single 2.5GbE port for Node 1 and 1GbE for the two EliteDesks.
details: Install the 2.5GbE PCIe NIC in Node 1
Cable all three nodes and confirm negotiated link speeds
Accept 1GbE on Nodes 2 and 3, sufficient for snapshot deltas and heartbeats

title: ZFS Replication Between Nodes
summary: Local pools per node with scheduled snapshot replication, trading a bounded data loss window for avoiding Ceph.
details: Configure replication jobs and set the interval
Document the resulting data loss window explicitly
Test cold migration between nodes
Verify HA restart behaviour on simulated node failure

title: Ollama and Open WebUI on the Passthrough VM
summary: The reason the P4000 was chosen: 8GB of VRAM fits a 7B to 8B model at Q4_K_M with context headroom.
details: Build the AI and media VM with the P4000 attached
Deploy Ollama and pull a 7B to 8B model at Q4_K_M quantization
Front it with Open WebUI
Confirm VRAM headroom under real conversation context

title: Jellyfin with Dual Transcode Paths
summary: NVENC on the passed through Quadro, with the iGPU Quick Sync block held as the fallback path.
details: Deploy Jellyfin on the same VM as the AI stack
Validate NVENC hardware transcoding through the P4000
Confirm the UHD 630 Quick Sync fallback path works
Mount media storage from the replicated ZFS pool

title: Day 1 Cutover Complete
summary: All three nodes in quorum, every service reachable through the tunnel, and Day 0 fully resolved.
details: Verify every service resolves through the Cloudflare Tunnel
Confirm no inbound ports remain open on the router
Run a full failover drill across the cluster
Close out the open Node 1 CPU decision in the Day 0 record
